title: Protect Research Notes: Storage, Sharing & Retention
description: Protect research notes with restricted sharing, a signed-out permission test, secret separation, redaction checks and a retention log.
h1: Protect Research Notes: Storage, Sharing & Retention
intro: A research notebook can expose more than the final report: source identities, copied personal data, account tokens and early guesses. Protect it by controlling what you collect, where it lives, who can open it and when copies are deleted. The procedure below is for a small authorized research project; it does not require running a username search.

sections.heading: 1. Separate observations from secrets
sections.body:
Create a case folder with three parts: a source log, restricted evidence, and a report draft, labeled with a neutral case ID like CASE-014 rather than a person's name.

Record the public URL, observation time with timezone, question answered, and confirmed-vs-uncertain status in the source log. Keep passwords, API keys, recovery codes, and session cookies out of all three parts, and crop unrelated emails or notifications before sharing screenshots.

sections.heading: 2. Restrict the storage and sharing route
sections.body:
Store research notes on a device with full-disk encryption, a screen lock, and current security updates, and restrict cloud workspaces to named collaborators with multifactor authentication.

Check whether a shared parent folder inherits access automatically, grant report readers access only to the report, and remove collaborators once work concludes. Disk encryption protects a locked device, not an unlocked laptop or active browser session.

sections.heading: 3. Test the permissions before storing evidence
sections.body:
Create a harmless dummy file first and paste its sharing link into a signed-out private browser window; if it opens without authentication, disable public sharing and retest.

Next verify that an intended collaborator can open only the agreed files. Include exported PDFs, attachments, local sync folders, and downloads in your review, because changing a cloud link never revokes copies already downloaded.

sections.heading: 4. Use a retention log, including backups
sections.body:
Write a retention decision before collecting anything: record the case owner, purpose, review date, and deletion trigger (for example, an illustrative 30-day post-report review).

At review, remove unnecessary screenshots, exports, and temporary copies from the recycle bin, version history, and email attachments. Record what stays and why, and allow immutable backup lifecycles to expire copies rather than promising instant erasure.

sections.heading: Worked example: a safe note and a risky note
sections.body:
A risky note dumps a copied profile, home address, guesses, and a session token into a public-link doc; a safer note logs CASE-014, source URL, IST timestamp, public bio clue, unresolved status, and review date.

Before exporting, search the draft for secrets, hidden comments, and identifying filenames, and inspect the exported PDF. A visual black box over selectable text is not true redaction.

sections.heading: If notes are accidentally exposed
sections.body:
Disable the exposed link immediately, revoke collaborator access where needed, and rotate any credentials or tokens that appeared inside the notebook.

Use workspace audit logs to determine which files were accessed and notify the project owner through your incident process. Keep a minimal incident record rather than forwarding the leaked notebook across extra channels.

faq.question: Should research notes contain passwords?
faq.answer: No. Store credentials in a dedicated secrets manager and reference their purpose without copying the value into the case.

faq.question: Does encryption make a public sharing link safe?
faq.answer: No. A service can decrypt a file for anyone permitted by its link settings. Test access separately from device encryption.

faq.question: Can MyRecon protect or delete my notes?
faq.answer: No. This is a storage and access-control workflow you carry out in your own tools. MyRecon does not administer your notebook or backups.
